# Slice48 CC execution and preflight

## Pre-edit contract readback

The assigned source is exactly `crates/nms-copilot/src/map/mod.rs` in the dedicated `workspace-coverage-contract` checkout at parent `3e8dd6b426d024adb9318497db49a35281b419cb`. Source editing and all product gates remain held until CDC explicitly acknowledges this source-cited readback. This record is within the ignored `workbench/slice48-return/` evidence allowlist.

The current `run_map` performs raw-mode setup, then grouped screen/cursor setup, constructs Ratatui `Terminal`, runs the borrowed model/session loop, and performs fail-fast teardown. Thus a setup `?` can skip cleanup, one failed cleanup can prevent later attempts, and a loop panic bypasses ordinary teardown. The loop body/signature, public signature, exports/imports, existing `no_run` example, and all other files are frozen. The implementation must keep `io::Result<()>` and the current result precedence: when explicit cleanup has an error it wins over either body result; when cleanup succeeds the body result is returned.

The private control owns three independent acquisition facts. Raw mode is marked acquired only after `enable_raw_mode` succeeds. Alternate-screen and cursor cleanup are marked attempted before their commands because a failed write may have partially changed the terminal. Constructor/setup failure unwinds through the already-constructed guard: `Drop` attempts only applicable restoration and cannot replace the original setup error. Explicit restoration disarms each applicable flag before calling it, computes disable/show/leave results in that order without early return, and combines them as `cleanup.and(body_result)`. This preserves cleanup-first precedence while still attempting every applicable operation once. `Drop` discards restoration errors and must not panic; it cannot guarantee restoration after OS failure, abort, process kill, forgotten guard, or a second panic during unwinding.

`run_map` will call the private orchestration with a statically dispatched Crossterm adapter; the closure constructs `CrosstermBackend(io::stdout())` and `Terminal`, then calls the byte-frozen `run_map_loop`. Rust drops the closure-local `Terminal` before the outer guard's explicit restoration. Ratatui `Terminal::drop` may itself call `show_cursor` when its internal hidden flag is set, so the map guard's operation trace is not a claim that the process emits only one cursor-show command. Its constructor delegates to `with_options` and can fail; the local guard already exists at that point. Ratatui's `hide_cursor`/`show_cursor` update its internal flag only after backend success. Crossterm 0.28 Unix raw-mode storage records prior settings only after successful mode change and clears them only after successful restoration. These facts support the chosen flags and ordering but do not establish physical terminal restoration.

The four requested inline tests use a private injected mock and exact literal traces: success covers the common eight entries; partial setup covers each failure twice (clean cleanup and all applicable cleanup failures); explicit cleanup enumerates the eight literal failure sets with both success and `Interrupted` body outcomes; unwind checks known panic payload preservation with successful and all-failing cleanup. `Rc<RefCell<_>>` exists only in the test fixture for trace observation. Owner strong-count and `control_drop` prove release. Injected traces establish the helper's control-flow contract only; real Crossterm, actual event/frame behavior, isolated native-PTY D0042 behavior, and module-floor reconciliation remain open for required Slice49 / higher-scale work.

Pinned dependency evidence: `ratatui-core-0.1.0/src/terminal/terminal.rs` Drop/new/hide/show; `crossterm-0.28.1/src/terminal.rs` public raw APIs; `crossterm-0.28.1/src/terminal/sys/unix.rs` raw-state save/restore.

The old example remains `no_run` because it needs a real interactive terminal. Public docs will describe attempted best-effort restoration, cleanup-first error selection, constructor/setup propagation, and unwind behavior without promising infallible recovery. The existing numeric `move_cursor` limit is unchanged. No panic hook, production catch, retry, dependency, terminal interaction, API, or concurrency policy is authorized.

The supplied helper `/private/tmp/nms-slice48-cc-capture.py` records argv, cwd, selected inherited environment and overrides, start time, pre-state, raw stdout/stderr bytes/base64/length/hash, child exit and end time before post-state parsing, and preserves working-tree identity.
